summary: This informational memo lists requirements for Layer 3 provider-provisioned virtual private networks, written from the perspective of the service provider. It applies to many different approaches a provider might use and is meant to guide the design of solutions.

eli5.summary: If a company wants a private network through a bigger network owned by someone else, there is a checklist of things it must do. This document is that checklist.

subtitle: A checklist of what customers and service providers need from a Layer 3 VPN service.

tldr.problem: Service providers could build Layer 3 VPNs in several different ways, and there was no common list for judging how well each approach meets real customer and provider needs.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the terminology, then lists requirements common to both sides, requirements from the customer view, requirements on the provider network, and management requirements.
tldr.outcome: It is meant as a checklist for evaluating each L3VPN approach, not for comparing approaches or for specifying the technical means of providing the service.

today: RFC 4031 is an Informational RFC, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated. It builds on the generic requirements in RFC 3809.

sections.title: Scope of the Requirements
sections.content:
RFC 4031 gives requirements specific to Layer 3 Virtual Private Networks (L3VPNs). A Provider Provisioned VPN (PPVPN) is one where the service provider takes part in managing and provisioning the VPN. Requirements shared with Layer 2 VPNs are in RFC 3809.

The document is a checklist: a consistent way to evaluate and record how well each approach satisfies each requirement. It does not compare approaches and does not specify the technical means of providing L3VPN service. It covers network-based (PE-based) VPNs, such as aggregated routing VPNs and virtual routers, and CE-based VPNs.

Four deployment scenarios are considered: Internet-wide, single provider with a single AS, single provider with multiple ASes, and cooperating providers.
sections.eli5: It is a report card for private-network services. Each approach gets checked against the same list, but nobody is ranked against anybody else.

sections.title: Sites, Customers and VPN Types
sections.content:
A site is a set of users with mutual IP reachability that does not depend on the provider's network. A customer is one organization that controls a set of sites, and an agent is a set of users the customer authorizes to manage its VPN service.

An intranet limits communication to the sites of one customer, such as branch offices reaching headquarters. An extranet allows communication between sites of different customers, such as companies cooperating on joint software development. A site is a member of at least one VPN and may belong to many.

Devices come in three kinds. A Customer Edge (CE) device faces the users at a customer site. A Provider Edge (PE) device faces the provider network and attaches to CEs over access connections. A Provider (P) device sits inside the provider network, has no direct CE attachment, keeps no VPN state and is VPN unaware.
sections.eli5: A company's offices are sites. If one company's offices talk to each other, that is an intranet. If two companies share some offices, that is an extranet. CE is the company's door, PE is the provider's door, and P is a road in between.

sections.title: PE-Based and CE-Based Tunnels
sections.content:
VPNs are built between CEs using access networks and tunnels, which encapsulate packets in another header. GRE, IPsec, IP-in-IP and MPLS are named as common examples. Putting one tunnel inside another makes a hierarchical tunnel.

In a PE-based L3VPN the PE holds a Virtual Forwarding Instance (VFI) for each VPN it serves. The VFI ends tunnels to other VFIs and ends the access connections from CEs, and holds the routing and forwarding information for that VPN. This supports separate forwarding and routing and overlapping address spaces. A PE can use a separate tunnel per VPN, or one shared hierarchical tunnel where the innermost header tells the PE which VPN a packet belongs to.

In a CE-based L3VPN a single tunnel level, such as IPsec, typically ends at pairs of CEs. The PE does not know which VPN a CE belongs to, and the VPN functions come from configuration on the CEs. The tunnel topology can be a full or partial mesh.
sections.eli5: In one design the provider's building keeps a separate mail room for each company. In the other, the companies seal their own packages and the provider only carries them without knowing who owns what.

sections.title: Common, Customer and Provider Requirements
sections.content:
Common requirements. Reachability information and data must be isolated to only the sites of a VPN, a site can be in multiple VPNs, and the internal structure of a VPN should not be discoverable from outside. A VPN solution must support IPv4 and IPv6 as both encapsulating and encapsulated protocol, and SHOULD be able to translate private or non-unique customer addresses for talking to public ones. On QoS, an L3VPN shall be able to support modes such as best effort (mandatory for all types), aggregate CE interface ("hose"), site-to-site ("pipe"), Intserv and Diffserv.

Customer requirements. Extranet membership needs approval by a customer agent of each organization. A VPN MUST be able to span multiple ASes and provider networks while appearing as a single homogeneous VPN, and SHOULD deliver the same SLA at all sites. Customers need several addressing schemes, including RFC 1918 private addresses and dynamically assigned ones. There SHOULD be no restriction on CE-to-PE routing protocols, and static routing, RIP, OSPF, IS-IS and BGP MUST at least be supported. The DSCP set by a user SHOULD be relayed transparently from ingress CE to egress CE.

Provider requirements. Providers need to support public and private IP addresses, IPv4 and IPv6, for unicast and multicast, and to assign address blocks from their own space so routes aggregate efficiently. Later sections cover identifiers, discovering VPN information, SLA and SLS support, routing, isolation, inter-AS VPNs, wholesale, tunneling, access and backbone technologies, protection and restoration, interoperability and migration.
sections.eli5: Everyone agrees the private road must stay private, work with old and new address styles, and let the company choose how its traffic is treated. The road owner also needs it to grow big without breaking.

sections.title: Service Provider Management
sections.content:
An SP and its customers MUST be able to manage the capabilities and characteristics of their VPN services, and automated operations and standard management platforms SHOULD be supported. A customer network management function lets a customer agent query or configure information, or receive alarms, about its own VPN. A provider network management function gives the provider a comparable view across all customers to help with troubleshooting, but it does not include confidential customer data such as keying material.

The management section covers fault management, configuration management (for PE-based and CE-based VPNs, routing, network access, security services, resource parameters, value-added services and hybrid services), accounting, performance management, security management and network management techniques.
sections.eli5: Both the company and the provider need a control panel. The company sees only its own network, while the provider can see enough to fix problems but not the company's secret keys.

sections.title: Security Requirements
sections.content:
The RFC separates traditional security needs (integrity, confidentiality, authentication) from isolation of VPN data and control traffic between specific sets of sites. Isolation can be seen as a form of security but is treated apart.

Customers SHOULD get a range of security features and MUST be able to add their own security on top of the provider's. Where a VPN runs over part of the Internet, it should offer a configurable option for standard IPsec methods: confidentiality, integrity, authentication and replay attack prevention. These MUST be configurable between CE-CE, PE-PE and CE-PE, and MAY use schemes including AES and 3DES.

A provider MUST offer authentication services for temporary user access, and network elements SHALL authenticate peers before providing a service. Sites may face denial of service and intrusion attempts from the public backbone, the Internet and temporary sites.
sections.eli5: The private road needs locks, ID checks and guards. The company can add its own extra locks, and the road crew must show ID before they work on it.
